name: badger
description: Traefik middleware authentication bouncer for Pangolin

documents.title: Introducción
documents.text: Pangolin Middleware: Badger Badger is a middleware plugin designed to work with Traefik in conjunction with Pangolin, an identity-aware reverse proxy and zero-trust VPN. Badger acts as an authentication bouncer, ensuring only authenticated and authorized requests are allowed through the proxy. [!NOTE] Badger can also be used standalone for IP handling (Cloudflare and custom proxy support) without Pangolin. Simply set disableForwardAuth: true in your configuration. See the Disabling Forward Auth section below for details. This plugin is required to be installed alongside Pangolin to enforce secure authentication and session management.

documents.title: Installation
documents.text: Badger is automatically installed with Pangolin. Learn how to install Pangolin in the Pangolin Documentation.

documents.title: Configuration
documents.text: Pangolin will provide the necessary configuration to Badger automatically via the HTTP provider. However, you can override the configuration settings by manually providing them in the Traefik config.

documents.title: Disabling Forward Auth
documents.text: To disable forward auth and only use IP handling, set disableForwardAuth: true . When enabled, all requests pass through without authentication, and the required configuration options above are not needed: Only do this if you do not need Pangolin's authentication features and only want IP handling.

documents.title: IP Handling Configuration
documents.text: Badger automatically extracts the real client IP from requests. By default, it trusts Cloudflare IP ranges and uses the CF-Connecting-IP header.

documents.title: Using with Cloudflare (Default)
documents.text: No additional configuration needed. Badger automatically: - Trusts Cloudflare IP ranges - Extracts IP from CF-Connecting-IP header - Sets X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-For headers for downstream services

documents.title: Using without Cloudflare
documents.text: If you're using a different proxy or load balancer, configure custom trusted IPs and/or a custom IP header: Ensure you always disable the default Cloudflare IP ranges by setting disableDefaultCFIPs: true and provide your own trusted IP ranges in CIDR format under trustip if using a different proxy.

documents.title: Updating Cloudflare IPs
documents.text: To update the Cloudflare IP ranges, run: This fetches the latest IP ranges from Cloudflare and updates ips/ips.go .
